subject: LumenForge pilot — request for benchmark carveout & MFN opt-out
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica@lumenforge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@lumenforge.com>, procurement@lumenforge.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW & pilot scope

Rachel — thanks for the updated SOW. A few quick items from procurement after legal review (redlines attached):

- MFN clause: procurement requires an MFN covering any lower commercial terms offered to comparable customers during the 12-month pilot + rollout period.
- Benchmarking: they want a contractual performance benchmark (90% throughput at p95 latency) and an automatic credit/penalty schedule if not met.
- Exclusivity-like language: they asked for a right-of-first-consideration (ROFC) for similar vertical deployments for 6 months.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept MFN + the hard benchmark? We like the team and product but need these in place to move to PO.

Attachments: LumenForge_Redlines_v3.docx

Best,
Jessica
Senior Vendor Manager
LumenForge

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@lumenforge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW & pilot scope

Jessica — really appreciate the quick review and transparent asks. We can proceed but need to flag three items for internal approval: MFN, a contractually-enforced hard benchmark with auto-credit, and ROFC (which reads like a soft exclusivity).

High-level thoughts:
- MFN: standard MFNs that require parity with all future commercial terms are high risk for us as a growing PLG motion. We can offer a scoped MFN that excludes promotions, limited-duration pilots, and channel partner offers; alternatively, an MFN with a floor (e.g., excludes discounts tied to volume commitments >3x current commit).
- Benchmark: we're happy to define performance SLOs, but automatic credit schedules require operational allowances (maintenance windows, known variability). We'd prefer a measurement plan + remediation commitments instead of automatic monetary credits for the pilot.
- ROFC: acceptable as a non-exclusive ROFC with defined timelines and market/geography carveouts; we cannot accept anything that restricts our ability to pursue other customers.

Marcus and I will run this with Deal Desk + Legal for a proposed mark that balances their needs and our risk. I'll share a proposed SOW update and a counter redline.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal + pricing)

Can you hold for a couple days while we escalate?

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW & pilot scope — Deal Desk review required

Team — thanks for the heads-up, Rachel. Quick internal note on risk and precedent:

1) MFN: We should avoid an open-ended customer-level MFN covering all future commercial terms — this sets a bad precedent for PLG incentives and enterprise discounts. Approve only if it's tightly scoped (pilot-only, excludes promos/channel/renewal-based uplift). If LumenForge insists on enterprise-wide MFN for 12 months, require a commercial concession (e.g., higher base price or a smaller onboarding discount).

2) Benchmark/penalty: For pilot we can agree SLOs with an operational measurement plan. Monetary credits for missed SLOs are acceptable but capped (recommend cap = 15% of monthly fees for pilot months; no recurring credits on subsequent enterprise deals). Also add standard force majeure & maintenance carveouts.

3) ROFC: We do not want exclusivity. Non-exclusive ROFC with 60-day decision window and defined scope (product lines, regions) is acceptable.

I'll need Legal to review specific language — Laura, can you weigh in on exact MFN phrasing and credit cap? Vivek, for anything outside these guardrails (e.g., uncapped MFN, unlimited credits, any exclusivity), I recommend escalation to exec for sign-off.

- Ben
Head of Deal Desk

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW & pilot scope — Legal redline suggestions

Following Ben's notes — legal recommendations below (high level):

- MFN: Use a scoped-MFN clause. Key points: applies only to the Pilot Term defined in the SOW; excludes channel/reseller agreements and time-limited promotional pricing; includes a notice-and-review mechanic (customer must notify if they believe a better term was offered; Redwood may cure by offering parity for same commitment levels). If customer insists on an enterprise-wide MFN, require executive approval and a compensating commercial concession.

- Performance benchmark & credits: Convert "automatic credit" into a measurement schedule + remediation steps. If remediation fails 3 consecutive monthly measurements, limited credits apply up to a 15% cap on the pilot monthly fee. Include measurement methodology (traffic profile, p95 window, agreed test harness) and maintenance windows. Avoid open-ended SLA liability.

- ROFC: Limit to non-binding right-of-first-consideration (non-exclusive) with 45-day decision window; exclude certain product verticals. Anything that reads like exclusivity is not acceptable.

If LumenForge pushes back on either MFN scope or the credit-capped approach, we need executive sign-off for either: (A) any MFN covering future enterprise terms; or (B) credits >15% or uncapped credits; or (C) any language that grants exclusivity or restricts go-to-market.

Vivek — would you review the proposed thresholds and confirm whether we have latitude for (i) a 10% additional onboarding discount in exchange for a pilot-limited MFN, or (ii) veto authority to decline MFN requests fully?

Thanks,
Laura
General Counsel

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW & pilot scope — Exec guidance

Thanks team — I reviewed the background and proposed guardrails. Executive position:

1) MFN: Approve a pilot-scoped MFN only. No enterprise-wide MFN. The scoped MFN must: (a) be tied to the Pilot Term in the SOW; (b) exclude channel/reseller/promo pricing; (c) include customer notice + Redwood cure window. In exchange, the AE can offer up to a one-time 10% onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) — no additional base price reduction.

2) Benchmark & credits: We will not accept uncapped automatic monetary credits. Accept measurement plan + remediation, with a capped credit equal to 15% of monthly pilot fees triggered only after 3 consecutive missed measurements. Legal to finalize exact language.

3) ROFC: Non-exclusive ROFC with a 45-day decision window and explicit scope carveouts is acceptable. No exclusivity or right to prevent Redwood from pursuing other customers.

Action items for AE/Deal Desk:
- Rachel/Marcus: send LumenForge a counter-redline implementing the scoped MFN, measurement plan (attach test harness details), and capped credit schedule.
- Ben/Laura: prepare short guidance text and a negotiation playbook item for other AEs (codify MFN as pilot-scoped only).
- Rachel: confirm prospect accepts trade (pilot-scoped MFN + 10% onboarding credit) or escalate if they demand broader MFN/uncapped credits.

I'll authorize the one-time 10% onboarding credit against the proposal ID LF-2027-0421 under these constraints. If LumenForge pushes for anything beyond these points, escalate back to me with the customer's exact proposed language and commercial ask.

— Vivek
CEO | Redwood Inference
